title: Market Run, Week 7
dek: Kendre Miller has the New Orleans backfield while Alvin Kamara's back heals, and he is the first claim of the week.
author: Chef Hazy
intro_md:
Updated Thu 4:55 PM ET: the rest-of-season ranks are refreshed. Baker Mayfield is QB29 rest of season and stays a 2 to 4 percent claim; Mike Washington Jr. is RB48 and stays a 5 to 10 percent claim; MarShawn Lloyd, Tyjae Spears and Tyler Allgeier stay drops.

Updated Thu 4:35 PM ET: Denver designated Jonah Coleman to return from IR and he practiced Wednesday, so stash him at 2 to 4 percent before his activation. Baker Mayfield practiced in full again Thursday and Todd Bowles picks the starter Friday; he stays a 2 to 4 percent claim. Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Week 7, so Bam Knight is the Arizona back to add at 1 to 3 percent.

Updated Thu 4:20 PM ET: Terrance Ferguson is expected to stay on IR past Week 8 with no return date, so he comes off the stash list; monitor his practice window opening. Tyler Higbee moves up to a 3 to 6 percent claim as the Rams tight end to own.

Updated Tue 8:35 PM ET: Todd Bowles is still planning for Jalon Daniels to start at CAR, so Baker Mayfield moves down to a 2 to 4 percent claim for Week 8 on, and San Francisco is bracing for Mike Evans to miss at ATL; monitor Wednesday's practice report.

Updated Tue 6:15 PM ET: Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon and is out for the season, per Dan Quinn; drop him, and Antonio Williams stays a 1 to 3 percent stash for Week 8.

Four teams are off in Week 7, Buffalo, Jacksonville, the Chargers and Washington, and the wire is fresh in three places: a Saints backfield, two receivers who just took over full-time roles, and a Rams offense without Davante Adams for 6 to 10 weeks. Baker Mayfield is also back on the shelf for anyone who lost Jalen Hurts.

Pass on a big claim for Mike Washington Jr. (LV) as a replacement for Ashton Jeanty. Washington took half the early downs, but Jeanty still played 58 percent of the snaps and out-touched him 14 to 10. Tre Tucker (LV) scored twice on 7 targets, and two long TDs is not a role; leave him on the wire. Ja'Kobi Lane (BAL) ran 58 percent of the routes for 5 targets off IR, and Rashod Bateman's coach said Bateman should be OK; that is a 0 to 2 percent add in deep leagues, not a claim.

FAAB ranges are percent of a 100 budget, written for 10 to 14 team leagues in full PPR. Rostered figures are from public waiver pages Tuesday morning; a blank means no clean number was available.
outro_md: The Menu lands Wednesday with every one of these players ranked for Week 7. Claims first, lineups after.

adds.why: Kendre Miller (NO) ran a season-high 20 times for 70 at NYG and played 32 snaps, the most of any Saints back. Alvin Kamara left in the second quarter with his back and sat the whole fourth, and Travis Etienne Jr. is on IR until after Week 8, so the early downs are Miller's vs PIT in Paris.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 10 to 20 percent of FAAB. The top add on the wire, the New Orleans lead back for at least two more weeks.

adds.why: Omar Cooper Jr. (NYJ) played 51 snaps, 82 percent, in his first game off IR at NE and caught 6 of 7 targets for 103 and a 48-yard TD; a second TD came back on a penalty. Adonai Mitchell is week to week after the finger procedure, so the No. 2 job behind Garrett Wilson is Cooper's vs MIA.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 6 to 12 percent of FAAB. A full-time receiver on 5 percent of rosters.

adds.why: Germie Bernard (PIT) drew 12 targets at TB and caught 11 for 87 and the overtime TD, a week after a team-high 9 vs IND. Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. are on IR, so DK Metcalf and Bernard are the Pittsburgh passing game for about a month.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 5 to 10 percent of FAAB. 21 targets in two weeks is a weekly PPR flex.

adds.why: Mike Washington Jr. (LV) played a season-high 35 percent of the snaps vs BUF and took half the early-down snaps, running 9 times for 43. Ashton Jeanty still played 58 percent and out-touched him 14 to 10, so this is a split, and Jeanty is not losing the job.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 5 to 10 percent of FAAB. RB48 rest of season for me; the handcuff with his own early-down work vs LAR.

adds.why: Keenan Allen (IND) led the Colts with 11 targets vs TEN and caught 8 for 82, after 9 in each of Weeks 4 and 5. Josh Downs had 4 for 40 on 8, and Tyler Warren hurt his groin in practice before Week 6 with no timeline; his practice reports this week decide how long Allen keeps the targets at MIN.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 4 to 8 percent of FAAB. Three straight weeks of volume makes him a PPR flex while Warren is out.

adds.why: Tyler Higbee (LAR) led the Rams' tight ends at 83 percent of the snaps vs ARI and went over 60 yards in three straight games before that. Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and is out 6 to 10 weeks, which frees about 7 targets a game at LV. Terrance Ferguson is expected to stay on IR past Week 8 with no return date, per Adam Schefter, so the job is Higbee's for longer.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 3 to 6 percent of FAAB. A weekly tight end while Adams is out, and the Rams tight end to own over Ferguson.

adds.why: Jaylin Noel (HOU) has caught all 12 of his targets for 233 yards over Weeks 4 to 6, including 4 for 107 and a TD at JAX on 63 percent of the routes. Houston plans to activate Tank Dell off IR for Week 7 vs NYG, and Dell shares the slot, with Marvin Harrison Jr. ramping up too. His route share vs NYG Sunday decides whether he stays on a roster.
adds.verdict: Add him, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB, and no more. A deep-league flex vs NYG before Houston's Week 8 bye.

adds.why: DeMario Douglas (NE) caught 7 of 8 targets for 86 and a TD vs NYJ, after 4 for 65 and 2 TDs vs LV. Romeo Doubs is on IR for at least four games and Mack Hollins sat, so the slot is Douglas' Thursday at CHI.
adds.verdict: Add him, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB, before Thursday night. A PPR flex while Doubs is out.

adds.why: Baker Mayfield (TB) practiced in full Wednesday and Thursday on the dislocated right thumb; the MRI showed no further damage and no surgery. Todd Bowles decides Friday whether Mayfield or Jalon Daniels starts at CAR. Emeka Egbuka turned 16 targets from Daniels into 48 yards in Week 6.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 2 to 4 percent of FAAB. QB29 rest of season for me, the first starting quarterback back on the wire.

adds.why: Bam Knight (ARI) ran 15 times for 80 at LAR on 32 snaps with Jeremiyah Love out, and got most of the red-zone touches. Tyler Allgeier played 40 snaps and ran 18 times for 38. Love did not practice Wednesday and is expected to miss Week 7.
adds.verdict: Add him, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB. He leads the early downs and the red-zone work vs DEN with Love out.

adds.why: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (NYG) scored twice on 8 touches vs NO on 38 percent of the snaps, while Cam Skattebo played 6 snaps with no touches. Devin Singletary played 40 percent and the Giants' backs ran 14 times for 34.
adds.verdict: Add him, 0 to 2 percent of FAAB. The Giants released Najee Harris Tuesday, so it is a three-back committee at HOU; he is the bench piece if John Harbaugh picks him.

adds.why: Michael Mayer (LV) caught 7 of 9 targets for 95 vs BUF, after 8 for 82 on 10 in Week 4, and Brock Bowers had no first-half targets in Week 6. Las Vegas plays two tight ends a lot.
adds.verdict: Stream him vs LAR, 0 to 2 percent of FAAB, if your tight end is on bye.

stashes.why: Jonah Coleman (DEN) went on IR Sep 26 with a high ankle sprain, and Denver designated him to return Wednesday; he practiced that day, which opens his 21-day window. He had 58 yards, 3 catches and a TD in his last game, and his activation cuts into J.K. Dobbins' early downs.
stashes.verdict: Stash him, 2 to 4 percent of FAAB, and hold him where he is rostered; his activation could come before Sunday at ARI.

stashes.why: Antonio Williams (WAS) led Washington's receivers in snaps and routes in Week 6. Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon Monday night and is out for the season, per Dan Quinn, and Washington is on bye in Week 7.
stashes.verdict: Stash him, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB. He lines up as the No. 1 outside receiver with McLaurin out when Washington returns in Week 8.

stashes.why: Konata Mumpfield (LAR) played 27 snaps as the third receiver vs ARI with Tutu Atwell a healthy scratch. Adams' 43 snaps go to Mumpfield and the tight ends now.
stashes.verdict: Stash him, 0 to 2 percent of FAAB. His snap share at LV decides whether he is a flex.

drops.why: Jalen Hurts (PHI) has a deep vein thrombosis with clots in both lungs, is on blood thinners with no contact allowed, and is expected to miss the rest of the season. Tanner McKee starts.
drops.verdict: Drop him in redraft for any add on this list.

drops.why: Romeo Doubs (NE) went on IR Monday with the shoulder and misses at least four games. WR54 rest of season for me.
drops.verdict: Drop him for any add unless you have an open IR spot.

drops.why: MarShawn Lloyd (GB) ran 8 times for 10 vs DAL and played 30 snaps to Pierre Strong Jr.'s 41. Josh Jacobs is off the exempt list and eligible, though Matt LaFleur would not commit to him playing at DET; Jacobs practiced Thursday in his first week back. Either way Strong has the snaps. RB55 rest of season for me.
drops.verdict: Drop him for any add on this list.

drops.why: Tyjae Spears (TEN) had 1 carry and 1 catch at IND a week after his 9-catch game, and Tony Pollard ran a season-high 19 times. RB47 rest of season for me.
drops.verdict: Drop him for any add on this list.

drops.why: Tyler Allgeier (ARI) ran 18 times for 38 at LAR with Jeremiyah Love out, and Bam Knight out-gained him on 15 carries and took the red-zone work. RB44 rest of season for me.
drops.verdict: Drop him for Knight or any add on this list.

mnf.text: San Francisco beat Washington 23-17 to go 6-0. Terry McLaurin (WAS) tore the patellar tendon in his left knee on a non-contact route in the first quarter, and Dan Quinn said Tuesday he is out for the season after surgery. Washington is on bye. Drop McLaurin for any add on the list, and stash Antonio Williams, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB.

Mike Evans (SF) left late in the second quarter with the Achilles, came back, and led San Francisco with 94 yards on 3 catches. Kyle Shanahan called it Achilles tendinitis and not a long-term problem, but NBC Sports Bay Area reports San Francisco is bracing for him to miss at ATL, with the bye in Week 8. WR23 rest of season for me. Monitor; Wednesday's practice report.
